Description - ModifyFolder

Changes folder properties. Verified live: name, password, hidden, adult, publicUpload and view.gallery change and are echoed in folderDetails. Omitted or nil parameters are left unchanged. Returns the folder after the change and the tree modify times.

**description, freePoints, freeTransfer: accepted and ignored on every observable path** (exercised live on sandbox folders that were empty or held one 201-byte own file, each value reverted). Any in-range value returns Ok and moves modifyTime (each prevModifyTime equals the previous call's modifyTime): 0, 1, 100, -1, 1048576 and 2147483647 (Int32.MaxValue) for the two numbers; plain text, Polish letters with XML-escaped markup, an empty string and 10,000 characters for description. Nothing is echoed (folderDetails keeps the three members nil), Folders never returns a value (also seen from the parent), and there is no effect on the owner's Download offer (own/0 before and with the fields set), on the anonymous public folder and file pages (openPublicFolderPage, openPublicFilePage) or on the balance (checked after every step). A non-numeric or empty freePoints/freeTransfer, and a freePoints of 2147483648 (one above Int32.MaxValue; not tried for freeTransfer), give HTTP 500 a:DeserializationFailed naming the parameter and its type System.Nullable<Int32>, raised before the operation runs; no application-level error was ever returned for these members. Whether the server writes them to a store that no interface reads: Unknown.

The client never sends them: its folder-options dialog has widgets for a description, free transfer (in MB) and free points, but they are hidden. Their meaning is Inferred from those widgets and the client's folder tooltip "This folder has %1 of free transfer.": transfer (kB) or points the folder owner sponsors for downloads, not a price.

The password sandbox-pass-123 in the examples is a throw-away value the capture tool set on its own sandbox folder (deleted afterwards), not a real folder password.

Client vs server (live): the 2.0.8.2 client sends its last flag as <public>, which the server does not know and silently ignores; the server parameter is publicUpload. The password is echoed back in plain text.

When the client sends it: folder options dialog (FolderOptions); only changed fields among name, password, hidden, adult and public are sent.

Routing. The path item declares the server http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=, so this operation resolves to http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/ModifyFolder. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the SOAPAction header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (.svc/ModifyFolder) does not work (a:DestinationUnreachable, see soapRestStylePath).

Wire format. POST with Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8 (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers text/xml; charset=utf-8) and SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/ModifyFolder (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (Content-Encoding: gzip).

Path notes

SOAP operation ModifyFolder. The path-level server makes the URL routable: WCF dispatches on SOAPAction and ignores the ?op=/ModifyFolder query.

Body required.

Body text/xml

Schema

Schema ModifyFolderRequestEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required ModifyFolderRequestEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 request envelope for ModifyFolder: <s:Envelope><s:Body><ModifyFolder xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/">…. No SOAP header is ever sent; xmlns:i is declared on the operation element only when a nil value is present.

    • @s:encodingStyle string optional = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/" namespace http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

      SOAP 1.1 encodingStyle attribute. The real client always writes it; the service accepts the envelope with or without it.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one operation element; no other content (this also makes the per-operation envelopes mutually exclusive).

      • <ModifyFolder> object required ModifyFolderRequest xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

        Operation element ModifyFolder in http://chomikuj.pl/ (trailing slash is mandatory: with http://chomikuj.pl the parameters are not matched, see Service/wrong-operation-namespace).

        • <token> string required Token

          Session token. Always the first child.

        • <folderId> integer (int32) required

          Folder to modify. An unknown id gives Error/FolderDoesntExists.

        • <name> string optional nullable (i:nil)

          New name.

        • <password> string optional nullable (i:nil)

          New folder password; empty string removes the password.

        • <hidden> boolean optional nullable (i:nil)

          Hide the folder.

        • <adult> boolean optional nullable (i:nil)

          Mark as adult content.

        • <public> boolean optional deprecated

          Client-only element. ChomikBox 2.0.8.2 sends its "public" flag under this name, but the server has no such parameter and silently ignores it (ModifyFolder/client-public-element-ignored: <public>0</public> was sent and publicUpload stayed true, its value from the preceding set-public-upload call). The server parameter is publicUpload. Documented so that captured client traffic validates.

        • <freePoints> integer (int32) optional nullable (i:nil)

          Server-only parameter of CLR type Nullable<Int32> (named in its DeserializationFailed fault), never sent by the client. Accepted and ignored: values in the Int32 range (0, 1, 100, -1 and 2147483647 observed) return Ok, are not echoed and have no observable effect. A value outside that range (2147483648), a non-numeric value or an empty element gives HTTP 500 a:DeserializationFailed (all Observed). minimum/maximum state the Int32 range. Meaning Inferred: points the folder owner sponsors (hidden "Free points" group in the client).

        • <freeTransfer> integer (int32) optional nullable (i:nil)

          Server-only parameter of CLR type Nullable<Int32> (named in its DeserializationFailed fault), never sent by the client. Accepted and ignored: values in the Int32 range (0, 1, -1, 1048576 and 2147483647 observed) return Ok, are not echoed and have no observable effect. A non-numeric value or an empty element gives HTTP 500 a:DeserializationFailed (Observed); a value outside the Int32 range was tried only for freePoints, and the same fault is expected here because the fault names the same CLR type (Inferred). minimum/maximum state the Int32 range. Meaning Inferred: transfer in kB the folder owner sponsors (hidden "Free transfer" group; kB as in FolderInfo).

        • <publicUpload> boolean optional nullable (i:nil)

          Allow uploads by others (server-only parameter; the client sends public instead). Verified live (set-public-upload).

        • <description> string optional nullable (i:nil)

          Server-only parameter, never sent by the client. Accepted and ignored: plain text, Polish letters with XML-escaped markup, an empty string and 10,000 characters all return Ok; the value is never echoed in folderDetails, never returned by Folders and not shown on the public pages.

        • <view> object optional nullable (i:nil) FolderView

          View options (server-only; never sent by the client).

          • <gallery> boolean required

            Show the folder as an image gallery on the web site.

Accepted but untested parameters (x-untested-parameters)

Parameters the service accepts that were not verified live
ParameterStatus
descriptionexercised live: accepted and ignored on every observable path (never echoed, never returned by Folders, not on the public pages); storage in a backend no interface reads: Unknown
freePointsexercised live: in-range values accepted and ignored (no echo, no effect on offers, pages or balance); out-of-range, non-numeric or empty values give a:DeserializationFailed; storage: Unknown
freeTransferexercised live: as freePoints, except that no out-of-range value was tried (same CLR type, same fault expected: Inferred)

Responses - 200, 500

200

SOAP response envelope. HTTP 200 is used for every service-level outcome, including errors: check ModifyFolderResult/status. Compressed (Content-Encoding: gzip) when the request accepts gzip.

Schema text/xml

Schema ModifyFolderResponseEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required ModifyFolderResponseEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 response envelope for ModifyFolder: <s:Envelope><s:Body><ModifyFolderResponse xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/"><ModifyFolderResult …>.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one response element; no other content.

      • <ModifyFolderResponse> object required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/
        • <ModifyFolderResult> object required ModifyFolderResult

          Result element; declares xmlns:i (XML Schema instance, for i:nil) and xmlns:a.

          • <a:status> string required Status xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Outcome of the call. The client accepts only Ok; BadToken triggers a re-login, anything else is an error.

            7 values
            • "Ok" Success. The only value the client treats as success.
            • "BadToken" Unknown, logged-out or otherwise invalid token. The client re-authenticates (Auth) once per message (message-relog-count=1) and resends the message with the new token; session-bound messages are dropped.
            • "Forbidden" Auth: user name does not exist. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "PermissionError" Auth: wrong password for an existing user. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "Error" Generic failure. Usually carries a reason in errorMessage (e.g. EmptyName, NameExistsAtDestination); FolderFiles with an unknown disposition returns Error with errorMessage nil (FolderFiles/invalid-disposition).
            • "NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder" RemoveFolder with force=false on a folder that contains files, or on an unknown/removed folder id.
            • "WrongDisposition" FolderFiles: the disposition is a known value but not allowed for this call (download).
          • <a:errorMessage> string required nullable (i:nil) ErrorMessage xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Error detail for status=Error; nil otherwise.

          • <a:folderDetails> object optional nullable (i:nil) FolderInfo xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            The folder after the change (for an unknown id: an echo of the requested values).

            • <id> integer (int32) required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Folder id (0 = account root).

            • <name> string optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Folder name (the account name for the root).

            • <passwd> boolean optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              The folder is password protected. With passwd=true and an empty password the client stores the placeholder password asd locally.

            • <hidden> boolean optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Hidden from other users.

            • <adult> boolean optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Marked as adult content.

            • <freePoints> integer (int64) optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Free points: nil in every response, also right after ModifyFolder set a value, and for all 586 folders of the test account. The client stores it without displaying it. Meaning Inferred: points the owner sponsors for downloads from this folder.

            • <freeTransfer> integer (int64) optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Free transfer in kB: nil in every response, as freePoints. The client multiplies it by 1024 and shows the folder tooltip "This folder has %1 of free transfer." when it is > 0; that never happened for the test account. Meaning Inferred: transfer the owner sponsors for downloads from this folder.

            • <publicUpload> boolean optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Other users may upload into the folder.

            • <folders> list optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Subfolders; nil when the requested depth is exhausted or the folder has no children.

              • <FolderInfo> object optional nullable (i:nil) repeated FolderInfo

                A folder of the account tree (FolderInfo), returned by Folders (folder, recursively in folders) and ModifyFolder (folderDetails). Members are unprefixed (namespace http://chomikuj.pl/) and in this order.

                Recursive: the same structure as FolderInfo above.

            • <password> string optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Folder password, echoed in plain text by the service when set (ModifyFolder/set-password); nil otherwise.

            • <view> object optional nullable (i:nil) FolderView xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              View options.

              • <gallery> boolean required

                Show the folder as an image gallery on the web site.

            • <description> string optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Folder description: nil in every response observed, even right after ModifyFolder set one. Not read by the client.

            • <chomikId> integer (int32) required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Owner hamster (account) id.

          • <a:prevModifyTime> integer (int64) required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Tree modification time before the call (ticks). If it differs from the local tree time the client refreshes with Folders(0,0).

          • <a:modifyTime> integer (int64) required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Tree modification time after the call (ticks).

The real client sends its last flag as <public>; the service has no such parameter (oracle) and silently ignores it: hidden changes, publicUpload does not.

500

WCF SOAP faults captured for this operation (HTTP 500, not compressed): a non-numeric or empty freePoints/freeTransfer, and a freePoints outside the Int32 range, give a:DeserializationFailed naming the parameter and its CLR type (System.Nullable<Int32>); the fault is raised during deserialisation, before the operation runs. Any SOAP operation can also give the generic faults of components.responses.SoapFault.

Schema text/xml

Schema SoapFaultEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required SoapFaultEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 fault envelope (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, never gzip-compressed).

    • <s:Body> object required
      • <s:Fault> object required SoapFault

        The fault.

        • <faultcode> string required no namespace

          Qualified fault code with its own namespace declaration on the element: a:InternalServiceFault and a:DeserializationFailed (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/net/2005/12/windowscommunicationfoundation/dispatcher), a:ActionNotSupported and a:DestinationUnreachable (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2005/05/addressing/none).

        • <faultstring> object required no namespace

          Human-readable message. DeserializationFailed names the parameter and CLR type, which is how the contract was established.

          • @xml:lang string required namespace http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace

            Language of the message (en-US).

          • text content string required

            Message text.

Client vs live - discrepancies

Where the client's expected behaviour and the live service disagree, the spec follows the live behaviour (x-discrepancies):

  • Client element public is not a server parameter (ignored); the server uses publicUpload.
  • Server-only parameters freePoints, freeTransfer, description and view{gallery}: the client never sends them. The first three are accepted and ignored live.

Security notes - findings that concern ModifyFolder

  • S-02 Medium Folder passwords are returned in plain text over HTTP: ModifyFolder echoes the new password, Folders lists each folder's password, and the folder created by SavePlaylist gets a server-generated password while passwd=false.
  • S-14 Info ModifyFolder accepts description, freePoints and freeTransfer and silently ignores them: any in-range value (including -1, Int32.MaxValue and a 10,000-character description) returns Ok and moves modifyTime, but nothing is echoed, Folders never returns a value, and no effect was visible in download offers, public pages or the balance. The client never sends these fields.

From x-security-notes in the spec. Ratings and scope are explained on Security & privacy.
